text:
Sam Chen: Heads-up, onboarding `lyra-14b-v1`. Legal uploaded the model README; looks like a hybrid CC-BY-NC-SA + dataset-specific clause that restricts certain commercial hosting.
Nina Alvarez: Ugh. Can you paste the exact clauses? NC + SA together usually means no commercial use and share-alike for derivatives.
Sam Chen: Pasted snippet from the README: "Weights and derived artifacts may not be used for commercial redistribution or hosted behind a paid API. Attribution required. Third-party dataset X restricts model shipping to academic/research only."
Leo Grant: Important Qs for infra: 1) If we quantize for Dedicated (internal only) is that a derivative that violates shipping restriction? 2) If we provide hosted API outputs (text/embeddings) is that considered "hosting behind a paid API"? 3) Do cached/prefetched KV shards count as redistribution?
license-bot: automated scan: license flags = ["noncommercial", "sharealike"], provenance flag = "third-party dataset restriction", action = "legal review recommended" :warning:
Maria Lopez: From product POV: customers expect we can serve models under Dedicated/Private if license allows. This one seems to block Hosted. We need to confirm whether Dedicated (reserved for customer) is considered "hosting behind a paid API".
Nina Alvarez: My read: NC (noncommercial) pretty clearly blocks charging for access. Dedicated with customer paying Redwood for infra might still be allowed if customer holds an enterprise license from upstream — but repo language forbids hosting derivatives commercially, unclear about customer-managed Private deployments.
Sam Chen: So two competing possibilities: - We can offer as Private (customer brings their own license, we don't host) - We cannot include in Redwood Hosted catalog or enable in Dedicated without explicit upstream permission.
Leo Grant: Concrete ask for legal: 1) Is quantized weights a derivative that triggers SA? 2) Does caching/serving embeddings count as "redistribution"? 3) If we only expose model via inference (no weight export) is that still "hosting behind a paid API"? Nina, can you file the ticket?
Nina Alvarez: Filed internal legal request: RL-8421 with priority high, added license text + sample use-cases (hosting, dedicated, private, cache). @license-bot added.
license-bot: RL-8421 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RL-8421 :link: Assigned to Legal Ops.
Maria Lopez: For UX: if Legal says Hosted is disallowed, we need a guardrail in the Console to prevent selecting the model for Hosted deployments and surface a tooltip with attribution copy if Private is allowed.
Sam Chen: Also capturing a runtime question: are we allowed to generate and store embeddings for customers (they pay us)? If NC blocks commercial use, we need explicit permission from upstream.
Leo Grant: On quantization: we should assume quantization = derivative until legal confirms otherwise. Do not create quantized redistributable assets in the repo or S3 buckets accessible to org outside legal-scoped work.
Nina Alvarez: Agreed. Until RL-8421 resolved: - no Hosted catalog listing - no public quantized artifacts - allow on-prem/private only with customer-signed upstream license or legal approval.
license-bot: quick checklist added to RL-8421: ["copy of upstream license", "clarify NC scope (commercial definitions)", "clarify SA effect on quantized artifacts", "clarify third-party dataset clause"]; ETA 3 business days.
Maria Lopez: I'll sketch the Console guardrail text: "This model's upstream license restricts commercial hosting. Contact Legal or supply signed upstream license to enable Hosted/Dedicated. Attribution required: "Model: Lyra-14B (Upstream author)"". Posting in the ticket.
Sam Chen: Thx. I'll hold off on benchmark runs that produce shareable artifacts. Will run evals internally but no artifacts outside protected buckets.
Leo Grant: I'll add a CI gate that blocks artifact publishing when model tag = lyra-14b until legal flag is cleared. PR to infra repo coming.
Nina Alvarez: Legal Ops acknowledged RL-8421 and requested example contracts where a customer might want Hosted access. Adding DS/SE notes.
Maria Lopez: Thanks team. We should update the onboarding checklist template to include a NC/SA quick flag so future models get flagged earlier.
Sam Chen: Agree. Minor note: can we add an automated rule in model-onboarding form to detect common license keywords (NC, SA, noncommercial, attribution) and auto-route to Legal? That would save time.
license-bot: feature request captured: MOG-129 (auto-license-routing). Added to backlog.
Nina Alvarez: Closing loop: until legal confirms, treat lyra-14b as research-only for Redwood Hosted and no redistributable deriv artifacts. I'll ping when RL-8421 updates.
Sam Chen: :thumbsup: End.
